title: Classic pivot zones — scale-aligned terminal-hazard test

dataset.analysis_timeframe: D/H1, W/H4, M/D1, Q/W1, Y/MN1 with H1 mismatch benchmarks
dataset.timezone: UTC source; NY17 DST-safe FX trading periods

hypotheses.market_question: Does pivot-proximity terminal hazard become more coherent when the directional-leg detector is scale-aligned to the pivot horizon instead of forcing all pivot horizons through H1 legs?
hypotheses.null: Occupancy-adjusted terminal-extreme incidence near classic pivots is not positively enriched after scale alignment and frozen cross-pair falsification.
hypotheses.alternative: At least one preregistered scale-aligned pivot/leg mapping shows stable positive terminal-hazard enrichment in the 0-20% pivot core versus the 30-50% outer region.
hypotheses.mechanism: If pivot relevance is horizon-dependent, the price-response horizon should scale with the period used to construct the pivot reference.

method.primary_endpoint: For D/H1, W/H4, M/D1, Q/W1 and Y/MN1: terminal_rate(0-20% normalized pivot spacing) minus terminal_rate(30-50%) using same-geometry high/low occupancy.
method.economic_effect_size: Percentage-point enrichment in independently confirmed ATR-defined terminal-extreme incidence per eligible high/low occupancy observation.
method.event_definition: Classic floor pivots from prior completed period. Directional termination is pivot-blind: ATR24 simple mean, lagged one detector bar, 0.75 ATR directional-change threshold, with a candidate extreme confirmable only by a strictly later detector candle.

inference.multiple_testing: Holm correction across five primary scale-aligned horizon hypotheses

execution.same_bar_policy: candidate endpoint cannot self-confirm on same detector candle

provenance.notes: Preregistration and two implementation clarifications were committed before outcome computation. Amendment 02 froze strict later-bar terminal confirmation to prevent wick circularity.
